description: Solo project working on be an earth system detective
summary: This project uses 10 years of NASA satellite thermal data and local GIS area measurements to study the Urban Heat Island effect in Lucknow , India. By comparing May 2016 and May 2026 daytime land surface temperature alongside dense concrete residential zones in Gomti Nagar , we identify priority neighborhoods for urban tree planting and cooling solutions.
details:
1. What It Does:

Our project tracks how rapid urban expansion and dense concrete construction contribute to extreme daytime surface heat in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Using open-access Earth observation tools, we bridge city-wide thermal satellite trends with neighborhood-level ground measurements to pinpoint where heat mitigation is needed most.

2. How We Built It (GIS Methodology):

• Satellite Thermal Trend Analysis: Using NASA Worldview, we analyzed Aqua/MODIS Land Surface Temperature (Day) data comparing May 2, 2016 and May 2, 2026 across central Uttar Pradesh. Daytime surface temperatures consistently reached 42°C to 52°C (315 K–325 K), with continuous orange high-heat zones expanding across the plains over the decade.

• Ground-Level Spatial Measurement: Using Google Earth high-resolution imagery (May 2026), we mapped and measured a densely built residential sector near Mini Sports Stadium in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow (26.85°N, 81.01°E). The measured built-up block covers 264,660.78 m² (0.265 sq km) with a perimeter of 2,058.51 m and minimal tree canopy.

3. Proposed Solutions & Impact:

Combining satellite heat maps with local GIS measurements gives city planners an affordable way to target cooling interventions, including native shade tree corridors along major avenues, reflective cool roofs on dense housing blocks, and neighborhood micro-park.

NASA Data & Space Agency Resources Used:

• NASA Worldview (Aqua/MODIS Land Surface Temperature Day — May 2, 2016 & May 2, 2026)

• Google Earth High-Resolution Satellite Imagery
